overall.note: Every open round 2 item is resolved or, for the reserved-space items, closed by an acceptable documented rationale; one partly. One new Minor (N3-01, Profile compact preview: CSS differs from the spec) keeps Profile at Ship with fixes. The other seven units ship.

issues.summary: On phones the compact preview's CSS differs from the spec. The spec keeps a visible 'How customers see you' heading and caption, and puts the alert slot with the action row before the preview. The CSS visually hides the caption and moves the alert slot after the card. Result: an unlabelled chat card floats under the form, and a save failure appears below the card, about 180 px from Save. The bubble also sits about 250 px under First name, not the spec's 150 px. Build it as specified.

reservedSpaceRationale.summary: Spec §1.5 rule 8 ('Why empty space is kept') states the rule, names every place it shows, gives the user benefit (saving, an error or a status never pushes content someone is reading or about to tap) and tells engineers not to collapse it. It is applied consistently and measured to hold (no shift across saved, failed, removed and waiting states). The cost is a looser rhythm, most visible on Profile at desktop (~150 px under the name hint) and in Preferences at 320 (~125 px gaps). That is a deliberate trade, not a defect, so PR-1, PR-4, SE-2, ST-2 and PF-1 are closed. Optional later refinement: drawing Cancel and Save as unavailable in the clean name form would give the largest gap content without breaking the rule.
